examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}-3\underset{\sim}{b}&=-3(4\underset{\sim}{i}-3\underset{\sim}{j})\\&=-12\underset{\sim}{i}+9\underset{\sim}{j}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}|-3\underset{\sim}{b}|&=\sqrt{(-12)^2+9^2}\\&=\sqrt{144+81}\\&=15\end{aligned}$

The negative scalar reverses direction; the magnitude remains positive.

examples.question_text: Given $\underset{\sim}{a}=3\underset{\sim}{i}+2\underset{\sim}{j}$ and $\underset{\sim}{b}=-2\underset{\sim}{i}+5\underset{\sim}{j}$, find the exact value of $|2\underset{\sim}{a}-\underset{\sim}{b}|$.

The vector $\underset{\sim}{v}=t\underset{\sim}{i}+6\underset{\sim}{j}$ has magnitude $10$.
(a) Find both possible values of $t$.
(b) Find $t$ if $t<0$.
A walker travels $8$ km east, then $5$ km north. Find the magnitude of the final displacement, correct to two decimal places.

coverage.summary: Authored six examples covering every distinct assessed method, using supplied booklet methods and different values. Assessments were read only for classification; their mathematics was not re-audited or altered. Questions and solutions are separate editable fields, with aligned working and a phantom gutter for the bare opening expression. Solution prose and mathematics inherit renderer blue. The contextual solution includes an editable, unshaded component diagram; final rendering and label-size verification remain for the capture stage.

examples.derivation: Squaring the components gives 36+81=117=9×13, so the exact magnitude is 3√13. This follows the supplied magnitude formula and exact-magnitude exercises.
Multiplication by −3 gives components (−12,9). Their squared sum is 144+81=225, giving magnitude 15. The negative multiplier reverses direction while the length remains positive.

Twice a has components (6,4); subtracting b=(−2,5) gives (8,−1). The magnitude is √(64+1)=√65. Combining components before calculating magnitude matches Development Q5. The bare opening expression has the required phantom equals gutter.
The magnitude condition gives √(t²+36)=10, hence t²=64 and t=±8. The condition t<0 selects −8. This follows the supplied unknown-component exercises without introducing unit-vector calculations.

The perpendicular journeys give displacement components (8,5) km. Its magnitude is √89 km=9.433981… km, which rounds to 9.43 km. The solution diagram connects (0,0) to (8,0) to (8,5), with the resultant directed from (0,0) to (8,5) and a correct right-angle marker.

The sum has components (6,8), so its magnitude is 10. The separate magnitudes are 6 and 8, whose sum is 14. Thus 10<14 proves the requested inequality by the separate-calculation method taught in Development Q10(c).
